Verifier R1 2026-10-15, independent re-check of data/instruments.md. Criterion 1 validated scales named with citations: UNMET for one scale - QPS, IRI-PT, RIBS, IOS, Marlowe-Crowne C, AQ-27 are named with correct citations, but the OMS-WA row (:41, and :64) still carries the claims open finding AF-data-3 objects to, unchanged since 2026-10-09: 23 items "settled", the 22-item count "not supported", and Study 3 fit "robust CFI 0.91, robust RMSEA 0.13". My own extended WebSearch today (summary level, pages not opened) relays Szeto, Dobson & Knaak 2019 (R2MR meta-analysis) describing the OMS-WA as a 22-item scale with five subscales, and relays the 2024 Lindsay et al. paper itself concluding that the 22-item OMS-WA is reliable and construct valid, while its Study 1 EFA gave 23 items; another summary says one item is optional in the final measure. So 22 vs 23 is unresolved and "22 not supported" is contradicted. A further extended search did not surface the CFI 0.91 / RMSEA 0.13 figures; they need an unverified label or removal. Criterion 2 pre / post / 30-day behavioural follow-up: met - T0, T1 same session, T2 day 30 (window 25-35), optional T3 day 56. Criterion 3 primary outcome is behaviour, not mood: met - AAI-verified at day 30, self-report secondary, mood/distress monitoring only. Sample size recomputed in python3: 2 x (1.96+0.8416)^2 x 0.75 x 1.2 / d^2 = 109.01 / 226.05 / 627.91 -> 110 / 227 / 628 completers; /0.7 -> 156 / 323 / 898 per arm; 312 / 646 / 1,796 total, all match. Gap to close (owner Tukey): at :41 and :64 say 22 or 23 items, unresolved (23 = 2024 Study 1 EFA; 22 = five-subscale version used in R2MR / Working Mind evaluations), drop "settled" and "not supported", label or remove CFI/RMSEA; then V03 :124/:185 must match (AF-science-8).
